Curve parameter estimates from a fitted model

Source: R/curve_params.R
curve_params.Rd

Reports the parameters of the concentration-response equation itself — top, bot, beta, nec, ec50, slope, d and f — with their credible intervals, one row per parameter per equation.

curve_params(object, summary = TRUE, xform = identity, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bayesnecfit'
curve_params(object, summary = TRUE, xform = identity, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bayesmanecfit'
curve_params(object, summary = TRUE, xform = identity, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bayesnechurdlefit'
curve_params(object, summary = TRUE, xform = identity, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bayesnecgroupfit'
curve_params(object, summary = TRUE, xform = identity, ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class bayesnecfit, bayesmanecfit, bayesnechurdlefit or bayesnecgroupfit.

summary

A logical vector of length 1. Whether to return the summary table (the default) or the underlying posterior draws.

xform

A function applied to nec and ec50, and to no other parameter. See Details.

...

Passed to the per-component and per-level calls by the bayesnechurdlefit and bayesnecgroupfit methods, and unused by the other two.

Value

With summary = TRUE, a data.frame with columns model, wi, dpar, link, parameter, Estimate, Q2.5 and Q97.5, ordered by decreasing wi and then by the parameter order given above.

Estimate is the posterior median and the interval is equal-tailed, which is what fixef(robust = TRUE) reports for the same fit. For a single-block threshold fit the nec row is therefore the same number nec returns; for a two-block fit nec() returns the combined threshold rather than either block's, and for a bayesmanecfit it returns the model-averaged estimate, neither of which is a row here.

wi is the model weight summary reports, under whichever method the set was weighted by — pseudo-BMA unless loo_controls asked for stacking. It is 1 for a bayesnecfit, which is the whole of its own set.

dpar is the brms distributional parameter the row belongs to: "mu" for every ordinary fit, and additionally "hu" or "zi" for a joint two-block fit from bnec(family = "hurdle_gamma") or "zero_inflated_beta". The two blocks of such a fit need not use the same equation — see the model_survival argument of bnec — so model names each block's own equation, and is NA for a second block whose equation cannot be identified from the fitted formula.

With summary = FALSE, a named list with one element per equation, each a draws-by-parameter matrix. A two-block fit names the second block's columns with the distributional parameter, as hu_top; a single-block fit has no prefixed columns. The list records the links of its fit in a link attribute, since a matrix of draws has no column to put them in. For a bayesmanecfit these are each equation's own draws in full, not the weighted subset nec(posterior = TRUE) returns, so they should not be pooled. A bayesnecgroupfit returns a list of those lists, one per level, because a matrix of draws has no column to keep the levels apart.

A bayesnechurdlefit returns one such object per component, as rhat and check_sampling do, because the two components are separate fits with separate parameters and the combined endpoint is not a curve with parameters of its own. A bayesnecgroupfit returns one table for the whole group, with a leading level column and sorted by level before weight, matching nec and ecx on that class.

Details

summary reports the model weights, the per-equation dispersion, the weighted no-effect estimate and the per-equation Bayesian R-squared. It does not report the parameters of the curve, and for a bayesmanecfit nothing else did either. Those parameters are what a methods section states alongside the threshold estimates: top is the control level the whole curve is referenced to, bot the asymptote a "relative" ECx is measured against, and beta the decay rate.

Only the parameters of the equation are reported. The family's own dispersion parameter is dispersion's and summary's, and a group-level term's standard deviation, its per-level deviations and the ogl offset are not parameters of the curve. Use fixef or as_draws_df on pull_brmsfit(x) for those.

The estimates are per equation and are not averaged across the set. The equations of a set do not share a parameter list: ecxexp has no bot, the three-parameter equations have no d, and only the equations of mod_groups$nec estimate nec. Averaging a parameter over whichever equations happen to estimate it would average over a different subset for each parameter, using weights that were computed for the whole set, so the weights of the rows contributing to one number would not sum to 1 and would sum to something different for the next number. The model weight is reported beside each row instead, so a reader can see what share of the model average each curve holds, and no quantity is reported that the weights do not support. See average_estimates for the estimates that are averaged.

show_params names the parameters of each equation without fitting anything; this function reports their estimates from a fit.

The parameters are on the scale the model was fitted on. bnec assigns link = "identity", so top and bot are on the response scale for every fit that did not name a link of its own. Where a link was named, brms applies its inverse to the whole non-linear expression, so top and bot are on the link scale. The link of each block is reported in the link column, and a message names any that is not the identity.

xform applies to nec and ec50 only. Those two are measured on the predictor axis, so where crf() transforms the predictor inline — crf(sqrt(x), ...) — they are on the transformed scale, exactly as nec and ecx are, and xform is the inverse that brings them back. Every other parameter is a response level or a shape parameter and is not on the predictor axis at all, so xform is not applied to it. Where the predictor is transformed inline and xform was left at identity, a message says which parameters are on the transformed scale.

See also

summary, show_params, nec, ecx, average_estimates

Examples

library(bayesnec)
data(manec_example)
curve_params(manec_example)
#>       model        wi dpar     link parameter   Estimate        Q2.5      Q97.5
#> 1 nec4param 0.8274318   mu identity       top  2.1683084   2.0515539  2.2620465
#> 2 nec4param 0.8274318   mu identity       bot -8.4184951 -13.5780477 -5.6830274
#> 3 nec4param 0.8274318   mu identity      beta -0.6709559  -1.1783599 -0.1954755
#> 4 nec4param 0.8274318   mu identity       nec  1.4610359   1.3608295  1.5277839
#> 5 ecx4param 0.1725682   mu identity       top  2.3077962   2.1421523  2.5009383
#> 6 ecx4param 0.1725682   mu identity       bot -5.6942272  -7.1930136 -4.0032952
#> 7 ecx4param 0.1725682   mu identity      beta  0.9580802   0.7073639  1.1674993
#> 8 ecx4param 0.1725682   mu identity      ec50  2.3535255   2.1455780  2.5540610
nec4param <- pull_out(manec_example, "nec4param")
#> Pulling out model(s): nec4param
curve_params(nec4param)
#>       model wi dpar     link parameter   Estimate       Q2.5      Q97.5
#> 1 nec4param  1   mu identity       top  2.1683084   2.051554  2.2620465
#> 2 nec4param  1   mu identity       bot -8.4184951 -13.578048 -5.6830274
#> 3 nec4param  1   mu identity      beta -0.6709559  -1.178360 -0.1954755
#> 4 nec4param  1   mu identity       nec  1.4610359   1.360830  1.5277839
